title: Week-ahead release intake and surge scenarios
notes:
Purpose: capture decisions for the upcoming week’s release train, codify hotfix intake flow, and outline surge scenarios + communication templates so oncall and release leads can act without ambiguity.

Timebox: 45 minutes.
Attendees: Ava Chen (chair), Miguel Torres, Priya Nair, Luke Adams, Sofia Martinez, oncall-rotation: Erin G. (observability).

Agenda:
- Quick status on queued releases and blocking PRs
- Hotfix intake: standardize triage -> canary -> ship path
- Surge scenarios: 3 escalation tiers and who owns them
- Canary thresholds & rollback criteria (metrics + time windows)
- Action items and next steps

1) Current queue summary (brief)
- Train A (target 2026-03-16): 5 releases, biggest is infra:split-kv-cache (PR #812). Blocker: integration test flakes REL-1721. Owner: Luke.
- Train B (target 2026-03-18): model-serving v2.3.1 (perf regression fix) staged, awaiting infra autoscale bump. Owner: Priya.
- Hotfix backlog: two P2 hotfix requests from customers (billing edge case, telemetry miscount). Intake IDs: REL-1734, REL-1736.

Discussion notes:
- Integration flakes for infra:split-kv-cache are likely due to testbed VM contention; temporary mitigation is to pin a smaller nodepool for the CI run. Luke to open infra ticket and add a CI tag to the PR to skip noisy suites.
- Priya confirmed autoscale config change is low-risk but needs a short window during which canary traffic will be diverted.
- Hotfix REL-1734 (billing): severity P2 -> agreed to expedite into next mid-week hotfix window (2026-03-12 20:00 UTC). Requirement: end-to-end test and manual billing smoke test.

2) Hotfix intake flow (canonical, use this every time)
Step 0: Intake posted to #release-ops with JIRA created and label "hotfix-intake" (oncall or SE can create).
Step 1: Triage in 30m by release lead: confirm severity, rollback plan, and owner. If P0/P1 escalate to Director on-call.
Step 2: Implement minimal patch on branch hotfix/<short-desc>. Add unit + smoke tests. Attach runbook stub in JIRA.
Step 3: Preflight checklist (docs + tests) completed; release lead confirms readiness.
Step 4: Canary rollout: 10% traffic for 15m, then 50% for 10m, then 100% if no alerts. Canary metrics: latency p95, error rate, 1-min QPS anomaly, and billing-count delta.
Step 5: Deploy to prod window. Post-deploy monitor for 30m with active observer assigned.
Step 6: Postmortem if outage or rollback; otherwise short ship note in #release-ops.

Minimum artifacts required at intake: JIRA ticket, short description, rollback steps, test links, owner, target window. Failure to provide these -> release lead rejects intake until completed.

3) Surge scenarios (three-tier escalation)
- Tier 1 (Controlled surge): traffic spike + marginal latency increase but within SLO. Owners: release lead + SRE. Actions: flip to burst-capacity auto-burst, enable heavier batching where possible, notify product (low urgency).
- Tier 2 (Degraded): sustained p95 > 2x target or error rate > 1%. Owners: SRE lead + Release manager. Actions: enable fallback model variant (if applicable), throttle non-essential routes, open major incident channel (#incident-ops). Escalate to Eng Director if persists > 15m.
- Tier 3 (Critical outage): complete degradation of inference or failed autoscale. Owners: Eng Director + CTO on-call. Actions: immediate rollback to previous model variant/version, activate on-call war room, initiate customer-facing status page update and support playbook.

Communication templates (use copy/paste)
- Preflight notice (to #release-ops and #product): "Planned hotfix REL-1734 scheduled 2026-03-12 20:00 UTC. Expected downtime: none. Canary 10% for 15m. Contact: Priya Nair."
- Incident brief (first 15m): "INCIDENT: service degradation affecting inference endpoints. Start: 2026-03-11 21:07 UTC. Symptoms: elevated p95 and 5xxs on /v1/generate. Oncall: Erin G. Mitigation: divert traffic to fallback pool. Next update in 10m."

4) Canary thresholds + rollback criteria
- Canary failure if any of the following during monitoring window:
  - p95 latency increases > 50% relative to baseline for > 5m
  - 5xx error rate > 0.5% (absolute) or > 3x baseline for > 3m
  - Any increase in billing counter delta > 1% unexplained by traffic
- If any threshold breached, automatic rollback initiated and release lead pages SRE.

5) Change log summary required for each train release (brief line per change)
- infra:split-kv-cache (PR #812) — adds partitioned KV caches to reduce redundant KV loads; risk: cache warming; mitigation: staged warmup and metric-backed gating. Owner: Luke Adams.
- model-serving v2.3.1 — fixes tokenization drift for code models; risk: perf regression; mitigation: canary profile and reduced max-batch for canary. Owner: Priya Nair.

Decisions made:
- Adopt standardized intake flow above as canonical for all hotfixes and P1/P2 releases until end of Q2.
- Canary windows standardized: 10% x15m, 50% x10m, 100% x30m with active observer.
- Surge Tier rules and paging matrix approved; Ops lead to add to runbook.

Action items (owner — due)
- Luke Adams — open CI nodepool pin ticket and add tag to PR #812 (due 2026-03-10).
- Priya Nair — schedule autoscale bump window and create canary traffic plan for v2.3.1 (due 2026-03-11).
- Miguel Torres — draft short hotfix intake template and add to Confluence page (due 2026-03-10). Linked artifact: confluence page id above.
- Erin G. — prepare observability dashboard for canary windows (add p95 / error / billing counter charts) (due 2026-03-11).
- Ava Chen — finalize communication templates and push to #release-ops pinned messages (due 2026-03-12).

Notes / open questions:
- Should we allow SEs to initiate hotfix intake for customer-reported billing issues without full E2E smoke tests? Consensus: temporary allowance if oncall approves and product supports, but must add manual smoke steps in JIRA.
- Consider adding an automated canary gate check (bot) that evaluates metrics and posts pass/fail before promoting traffic. Miguel to prototype.

Next meeting: pre-release triage (ad-hoc) on 2026-03-11 16:00 UTC to finalize windows for the week. Weekly release retro scheduled 2026-03-19, 09:00 UTC.

Attachments / references: links in linked_artifacts above.

Recorded decisions and action items should be copied into the release runbook and into the weekly release handoff doc.
summary: Weekly release engineering standup focused on standardizing hotfix intake, defining surge tiers, and locking canary thresholds. Agreed action items for infra and observability owners; canonical intake flow adopted until Q2 end.
next_steps: Owners to complete action items; Miguel to prototype automated canary gate; final comms pinned in #release-ops before first hotfix window.
